name: Saudi Arabia
summary: The world's swing oil producer and de facto leader of OPEC+, pursuing rapid economic diversification under Vision 2030. Riyadh balances security reliance on Washington with deep trade ties to China, and signed a mutual defence pact with Pakistan in 2025.
strategicInterests: Oil-market management through OPEC+
Vision 2030 diversification and giga-projects
US security guarantees and advanced arms
Détente with Iran and an exit from the Yemen war
Normalisation with Israel conditioned on a path to Palestinian statehood

government.notes: The crown prince serves as prime minister and is the kingdom's de facto ruler.

resources.name: Oil
resources.note: ~267 billion barrels; largest spare production capacity

resources.name: Public Investment Fund
resources.note: Sovereign wealth fund approaching $1 trillion

resources.name: Phosphate & minerals
resources.note: Ma'aden developing mining as the 'third pillar' of industry

name: Iran
summary: A revolutionary theocracy with major hydrocarbon reserves and influence over the Strait of Hormuz. Its regional 'Axis of Resistance' was badly weakened in 2024–25, and Israeli and US strikes in June 2025 damaged its nuclear programme, which had enriched uranium to 60%.
strategicInterests: Regime security and deterrence against Israel and the US
Preserve nuclear latency while seeking sanctions relief
Rebuild the network of regional partners and proxies
Oil exports to China despite sanctions
Strategic partnerships with Russia and China

capabilities: Largest ballistic-missile arsenal in the Middle East
IRGC Navy fast-attack craft and mines

government.notes: Ultimate authority rests with the Supreme Leader; the IRGC holds vast political and economic power.

resources.name: Natural gas
resources.note: Second-largest reserves (South Pars, shared with Qatar)

resources.name: Oil
resources.note: Top-five proven reserves

resources.name: Strait of Hormuz
resources.note: ~20% of global oil passes along its coast

name: Israel
summary: A technologically advanced military power and undeclared nuclear state that has fought on multiple fronts since the Hamas attack of 7 October 2023 — Gaza, Lebanon, Syria, Yemen and Iran. A US-brokered ceasefire in Gaza took effect in October 2025.
strategicInterests: Prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons
Security on the Gaza, Lebanese and Syrian fronts
Preserve the US alliance and qualitative military edge
Expand normalisation (Abraham Accords, Saudi Arabia)

capabilities: Multi-layer air defence (Iron Dome, David's Sling, Arrow)

government.notes: Right-wing coalition; next Knesset election due by October 2026.

resources.name: Offshore gas
resources.note: Leviathan and Tamar fields export to Egypt and Jordan

resources.name: Technology ecosystem
resources.note: Highest R&D spending as a share of GDP globally

name: Palestine
summary: The West Bank and Gaza Strip, recognised as a state by roughly three-quarters of UN members — including the UK, France, Canada and Australia in September 2025. The Gaza war since October 2023 caused catastrophic loss of life and destruction; a ceasefire began in October 2025.
strategicInterests: Statehood and an end to occupation
Humanitarian relief and reconstruction of Gaza
Palestinian political unity and governance reform
Full UN membership (currently a non-member observer state)

government.system: Semi-presidential (Palestinian Authority); de facto divided since 2007
government.notes: Hamas governed Gaza from 2007; post-war governance arrangements are contested.

resources.name: Gaza Marine gas field
resources.note: Discovered 1999; never developed

resources.name: Agriculture
resources.note: Olives and Jordan Valley farmland

name: United Arab Emirates
summary: A Gulf trade, finance and logistics hub with outsized geopolitical reach through sovereign wealth, ports and security partnerships stretching across the Red Sea and Africa. It is a leading investor in AI infrastructure.
strategicInterests: Global logistics and ports network (DP World, AD Ports)
AI and advanced-technology partnerships with the US
Influence in the Horn of Africa, Red Sea and Libya
Abraham Accords relationship with Israel

capabilities: Expeditionary experience in Yemen and Libya

government.notes: Federation of seven emirates; Abu Dhabi dominates.

resources.name: Oil
resources.note: ~100 billion barrels of reserves

resources.name: Sovereign wealth
resources.note: ADIA, Mubadala and ADQ manage well over $1.5 trillion

resources.name: Jebel Ali port
resources.note: Largest port in the Middle East

name: Qatar
summary: A small, extremely wealthy LNG superpower that punches above its weight as a mediator — in Gaza, Afghanistan, and between Russia and Ukraine. It hosts Al Udeid, the largest US military base in the Middle East.
strategicInterests: Expand LNG capacity and lock in long-term contracts
Mediation diplomacy as a source of influence and protection
US security partnership (Major Non-NATO Ally)
Gas field shared with Iran

capabilities: Hosts Al Udeid Air Base (US CENTCOM forward HQ)

government.headOfState: Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani
government.notes: The prime minister also serves as foreign minister.

resources.name: North Field gas
resources.note: World's largest non-associated gas field; LNG expansion to 142 mtpa

resources.name: Qatar Investment Authority
resources.note: Sovereign fund of roughly $500 billion

name: Egypt
summary: The Arab world's most populous country, controlling the Suez Canal and bordering Gaza, Libya and Sudan. A chronic economic crisis has been cushioned by IMF, EU and Gulf financing, while Houthi attacks slashed canal revenues.
strategicInterests: Nile water security against Ethiopia's GERD
Border security and mediation on Gaza
Restore Suez Canal traffic and revenue
Stability in Sudan and Libya
External financing to avert a debt crisis

capabilities: Largest army in the Arab world

government.notes: Military plays a central political and economic role.

resources.name: Suez Canal
resources.note: ~12% of global trade in normal times

resources.name: Natural gas
resources.note: Zohr field; now a net LNG importer again

resources.name: Nile
resources.note: Provides ~97% of Egypt's freshwater

name: Iraq
summary: OPEC's second-largest producer, balancing between the United States and Iran. Iran-aligned militias in the Popular Mobilisation Forces wield significant power, while the US-led coalition mission is winding down by 2026.
strategicInterests: Balance relations with Washington and Tehran
Assert state control over armed factions
Resolve oil-export disputes with the Kurdistan Region
The Development Road rail and highway link to Turkey
Water security as upstream dams reduce Tigris–Euphrates flows

government.notes: Parliamentary election held November 2025; ethno-sectarian power-sharing.

resources.name: Oil
resources.note: ~145 billion barrels — fifth-largest reserves

resources.name: Associated gas
resources.note: Much still flared; Iraq imports Iranian gas for power

name: Syria
summary: Emerging from 13 years of civil war after the Assad regime fell in December 2024. A transitional government led by Ahmed al-Sharaa is seeking sanctions relief and reconstruction funds, while integrating Kurdish-led forces and managing sectarian violence and Israeli military activity in the south.
strategicInterests: Sanctions relief and reconstruction financing
National unification, including the Kurdish-led SDF
Security arrangements with Israel
Return of refugees and internally displaced people
Future of Russian bases at Tartus and Hmeimim

capabilities: New national army formed from former rebel factions
Much former regime equipment destroyed by Israeli strikes (Dec 2024)

government.notes: Interim constitutional declaration adopted in March 2025 for a five-year transition.

resources.name: Oil & gas
resources.note: North-eastern fields; production far below pre-war levels

resources.name: Phosphates
resources.note: Significant reserves near Palmyra

resources.name: Mediterranean ports
resources.note: Tartus and Latakia

name: Algeria
summary: Africa's largest country and a major pipeline-gas supplier to southern Europe. Algeria backs the Polisario Front on Western Sahara, has severed ties with Morocco, and faces instability on its Sahel borders.
strategicInterests: Support Sahrawi self-determination in Western Sahara
Gas partnerships with Italy and Spain
Security on the Sahel frontier (Mali, Niger)
Non-alignment with ties to Russia and China

government.notes: The military establishment remains highly influential.

resources.name: Natural gas
resources.note: Pipelines to Italy (TransMed) and Spain (Medgaz)

resources.name: Iron ore
resources.note: Gara Djebilet deposit being developed

resources.name: Solar potential
resources.note: Among the highest irradiation levels globally

name: Morocco
summary: A stable monarchy with the world's largest phosphate reserves, positioning itself as Africa's gateway for European and Gulf investment. It has won growing international backing for its autonomy plan for Western Sahara.
strategicInterests: International recognition of sovereignty over Western Sahara
Atlantic Initiative giving Sahel states ocean access
Industrial hub for autos, batteries and green hydrogen
Nigeria–Morocco gas pipeline
Co-hosting the 2030 FIFA World Cup

government.notes: The king retains decisive powers over foreign, security and religious affairs.

resources.name: Phosphates
resources.note: ~70% of global reserves (OCP Group)

resources.name: Tanger Med
resources.note: Largest container port in the Mediterranean and Africa

name: Yemen

Government: restore state authority with Saudi and Emirati support
Southern Transitional Council: autonomy or independence for the south
Humanitarian relief for one of the world's worst crises

capabilities: Houthi anti-ship missiles, drones and naval drones

government.system: Contested — Presidential Leadership Council vs. Houthi administration
government.notes: The Houthis (Ansar Allah) govern Sanaa and the north-west.
